echo-and-narcissus-poussin

The handsome Narcissus lies by a pool, in love with his own reflection, while the nymph Echo fades away behind him. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1629, and in the myth Narcissus is turned into a flower.
esther-before-ahasuerus

Queen Esther, in a rich blue gown, faints in front of the king when she asks him to save her people, and the king rushes to hold her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1629, and the golden clothes and curtains are painted with care.
saint-bonaventure-s-body-lying-in-state
The body of a saint lies on a bier while a group of people in rich robes stand around, in a hushed, solemn room. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1629, as part of a series about the saint.
the-vision-of-the-blessed-hermann-joseph
A young monk kneels and holds out a ring to the baby Jesus and Mary in the sky, who reach down to him. Anthony van Dyck painted it in 1629.
apollo-in-the-forge-of-vulcan

The god Apollo arrives at a smithy to tell the blacksmith god, Vulcan, that his wife has been unfaithful, and everyone stops their work to stare. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1630, and the hard-working men are shown as real, muscular workers.
crucifixion-dyck
Christ hangs on the cross against a stormy sky, with Mary Magdalene kneeling at the base. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1630.
democritus

A man with a big smile and a curly beard, holding a pair of compasses, looks out at us with his eyes crinkling. Jusepe de Ribera painted this Greek philosopher in 1630, who was known as the Laughing Philosopher.
equestrian-portrait-of-charles-i-dyck

A king rides a large horse in front of a big tree, in armor, looking small but proud. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I of England in about 1630, and it was meant to make the king look tall, though he was short.
lot-and-his-daughters
A man sits with a cup in his hand as two women look at him, in a story from the Bible. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1630.
parnassus-poussin

The god Apollo sits at the center of Mount Parnassus, surrounded by the Muses and poets, who write and sing. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1630, and the graceful figures stand in a calm, balanced group.
saint-agatha

A young woman in a blue and yellow dress holds a plate with her own breasts, which is the sign of Saint Agatha, with a calm look on her face. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1630, and she looks out as if nothing is wrong.
saint-margaret-of-antioch
A young shepherdess in a beautiful dress holds a palm and a small dragon on a leash. Francisco de Zurbarán painted Saint Margaret in about 1630, and she looks like a real girl of the time.
samson-and-delilah-dyck
The strong man Samson lies asleep as soldiers creep in to capture him, while Delilah looks on. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1630.
self-portrait-as-the-allegory-of-painting
A woman in a green dress leans over her canvas with a brush in one hand and a palette in the other, concentrating hard. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself as Painting in about 1630.
self-portrait-by-judith-leyster

A young woman painter sits at her easel with a brush, turns around and grins as a fiddler stands in her picture. Judith Leyster painted herself in about 1630, and she was one of the few women in the Dutch painters' guild.
the-fortune-teller-tour
A young man is being charmed by a fortune teller while the women around him quietly steal his purse and cut his coin pouch. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1630.
the-garden-of-love
Elegant couples relax in a garden with Cupids flying overhead, among statues and a fountain. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1630, and his second wife, Helena, is one of the women.
the-lovers
A young man and a woman in rich Persian clothes sit close together, and she offers him a cup of wine. Reza Abbasi painted it in about 1630, and he was one of the most famous painters in Persia.
the-plague-at-ashdod
People in a city square stagger and fall in a plague, holding their noses, while a rat runs across the street. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1630, and it is based on a Bible story.
the-three-graces

Three plump women stand with their arms around each other, in a flower garden with a golden light. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1630, and the Three Graces are the goddesses of charm and beauty.
venus-asks-vulcan-to-cast-arms-for-her-son-aeneas
The goddess Venus asks the blacksmith god, Vulcan, to make armor for her son, as helpers hammer metal in the forge. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1630.
magdalena-ventura-with-her-husband-and-son

A woman with a full beard nurses a baby, while her husband stands behind her, and a long Latin text describes her story. Jusepe de Ribera painted her in 1631 because she was famous for having a beard, and he painted her with dignity.
portrait-of-an-old-woman-reading
An old woman with a wrinkled face reads a large book, and the light glows on the pages. Gerrit Dou painted it in 1631, and it's a student work of Rembrandt, painted with tiny, delicate brushes.
prince-balthasar-charles-with-a-dwarf

A small prince in a rich red suit stands next to a court dwarf who is holding an apple and a rattle. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1631, and the prince was the heir to the Spanish throne, but he died at 16.
saint-andrew
An old man with a white beard and a big wooden cross looks calmly at the viewer. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1631, and the saint's face is full of wrinkles.
the-apotheosis-of-st-thomas-of-aquino
Thomas Aquinas, a great scholar, floats in the clouds as saints and monks gather around him and the Pope and the Emperor kneel below. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1631.
the-proposition
A man offers coins to a woman who is sewing by candlelight, and she ignores him. Judith Leyster painted it in 1631, and it is a picture that says that a good woman will not be tempted by money.
christ-crucified-velazquez
Christ hangs peacefully on the cross against a dark background, with his head bowed. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1632, and it is quiet and calm.
portrait-of-jacob-de-gheyn-iii
A young man with a thin mustache and a white collar looks out with a faint smile. Rembrandt painted it in 1632, and the portrait has been stolen from a London museum four times.
self-portrait-with-a-sunflower
A man in a black coat and a gold chain points to a big sunflower, as if showing off his talent. Anthony van Dyck painted himself in about 1632, soon after he became court painter to Charles I.
the-abduction-of-europa
A princess sits on a bull that carries her into the sea, while her friends cry on the beach. Rembrandt painted it in 1632, and the bull is really the god Zeus, the king of the gods.
the-anatomy-lesson-of-dr-nicolaes-tulp
A doctor with a hat demonstrates the muscles of an arm on a dead body, while seven men lean in to watch. Rembrandt painted it in 1632, when he was only 26, and it made him famous in Amsterdam.
lot-and-his-daughters-vouet
A man is shown with two women who are filling his cup, with a bundle and a burning city behind. Simon Vouet painted it in about 1633.
militia-company-of-district-xi-under-the-command-of-cap

A company of Amsterdam's citizen soldiers pose around a table in dark clothes and colored sashes, some standing, some sitting. Frans Hals and Pieter Codde painted it between 1633 and 1637, and each man has a different expression.
still-life-with-lemons-oranges-and-a-rose
A plate of lemons, a basket of oranges and a cup of water with a rose are lined up on a table against a black background. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1633, and each object glows.
the-storm-on-the-sea-of-galilee

Christ's disciples struggle in a small boat in a huge storm, while Christ sleeps in the back. Rembrandt painted it in 1633, and it is his only seascape. It was stolen in 1990 and has never been found, so this is the only way to see it.
the-young-virgin
A young girl sits with her hands clasped, praying, in a quiet room, looking calmly at the sky. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1633, and her face is sweet and thoughtful.
watching-the-hunt-in-aranjuez

A group of the king's ladies and gentlemen in carriages and on horses watch the hunt in the gardens of a royal palace. Juan Bautista Martínez del Mazo painted it in about 1633, and he was Velázquez's son-in-law.
flora-rembrandt

A young woman in a rich dress, with flowers in her hair and a staff of flowers in her hand, looks out gently. Rembrandt painted it in 1634, and she is probably his wife, Saskia, dressed as the goddess of flowers.
hercules-and-the-hydra
The hero Hercules fights the many-headed hydra monster with his club, while it winds around his arm. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634 for a king's palace.
hercules-fighting-the-nemean-lion
The hero Hercules fights a lion, with his bare hands wrapped around its neck. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634, for a series of the Labors of Hercules.
hercules-separates-mounts-calpe-and-abylla
The hero Hercules pushes apart two mountains at the entrance of the Mediterranean, making the Strait of Gibraltar. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634, and the story is from legend.
judith-at-the-banquet-of-holofernes
Judith sits at a feast with the enemy general and hides her plan with a smile, while a table full of food is behind them. Rembrandt painted this in 1634.
the-adoration-of-the-golden-calf
People dance and sing around a golden calf while Moses, in the distance, comes down from the mountain with the tablets. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1634, and the colors are rich.
the-death-of-hercules
The hero Hercules writhes on a flaming pyre, dying from a poisoned robe. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634.
the-defense-of-cadiz-against-the-english
Spanish officers stand in a large, grand council room, talking about how to defend the port against the English fleet. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1634.
a-dance-to-the-music-of-time

Four figures, the Seasons, hold hands and dance in a circle to music played by an old man, Time, while a baby blows bubbles, and the sun god rides by in the sky. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1635.
agnus-dei
A lamb with its feet tied lies on a stone slab, against a black background, looking calmly at you. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1635, and the lamb stands for Christ.
charles-i-at-the-hunt

A king stands relaxed with a walking stick, with his horse and groom behind him, in front of an open landscape. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I in 1635, in a pose that was meant to look easy and royal.
charles-i-in-three-positions-dyck
A king's head is shown from three angles on the same canvas, left, front and right. Anthony van Dyck painted this in 1635 to send to a sculptor in Rome, so that he could make a bust.
rembrandt-and-saskia-in-the-parable-of-the-prodigal-son
A young man in a big hat holds a glass up and laughs, with his wife on his lap, as they pose as the Prodigal Son having a party. Rembrandt painted himself and his wife, Saskia, in about 1635.
saint-cecilia
A young woman in a gold and blue dress sits at an organ, with angels around her, singing. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1635, and Saint Cecilia is the patron saint of music.
saint-elizabeth-of-portugal
A queen in a rich gown stands with her arm raised and flowers in her lap, in a story about a miracle in which bread turned to roses. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1635.
the-cheat-with-the-ace-of-diamonds

A young man at a card table is being cheated by a woman, a maid and a man with a card hidden behind his back, with everyone glancing at each other. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1635, and the sly looks make it so funny.
the-feast-of-the-gods-bijlert
Gods and goddesses gather for a feast on a hilltop, with fruit, wine and music. Jan van Bijlert painted it in about 1635.
the-flight-into-egypt-lorrain
Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus travel through a golden valley, with a gentle morning light on the trees. Claude Lorrain painted it in about 1635.
the-surrender-of-breda-velazquez

A Spanish general holds out his hand to a Dutch commander who is handing over the keys to a city, with a forest of spears behind. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1635, and instead of boasting, the winner is shown being kind to the loser.
belshazzar-s-feast

A king and his guests are frightened by a glowing hand that writes a mysterious message on the wall in the middle of a feast. Rembrandt painted it in about 1636, and the words, in Hebrew, say that his reign is over.
charles-i-1600-1649-with-m-de-st-antoine
A king rides a large white horse under an arch, with his master of horse beside him. Anthony van Dyck painted Charles I in 1636, and the arch makes him look like an ancient emperor.
danae-rembrandt

A young woman lies on a bed with a golden glow, reaching her hand out as she greets the god Zeus, who comes as a shower of gold. Rembrandt painted it in 1636. In 1985, someone threw acid on it in a museum, and it had to be restored.
women-gladiators
Two women fight in a ring in front of a big crowd, in a strange painting. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1636, and it may show gladiators or a Roman festival.
apollo-flaying-marsyas
The god Apollo punishes a satyr, Marsyas, who dared to challenge him to a music contest, while others gather round. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1637, and the Greek myth is dark and gruesome.
aristotle
An old man with a long beard and a dark robe looks out with deep eyes and a lined face. Jusepe de Ribera painted the philosopher in 1637.
isaac-and-jacob
An old, blind man, Isaac, touches the hand of his son Jacob, who is pretending to be his brother, to get his blessing. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1637.
saint-apollonia
A young woman in a rich dress holds a pair of pincers with a tooth in them, the sign of Saint Apollonia, and a palm branch. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1637.
the-origin-of-the-milky-way-rubens
The goddess Juno pushes baby Hercules away, and her milk sprays across the sky, making the Milky Way, while Jupiter looks on. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1637.
the-rape-of-ganymede
A giant eagle carries the baby Ganymede up into the sky, with his arms outstretched. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in 1637, and the eagle is the god Zeus in disguise.
the-repentant-magdalen
Mary Magdalene sits in a dark room with a candle, a skull in her lap and her hand on it, deep in thought. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1637, and the candle is the only light.
et-in-arcadia-ego-poussin

Shepherds in a rocky landscape find a tomb with the words Et in Arcadia ego, a reminder that death is present even in happy places. Nicolas Poussin painted this famous picture in about 1638, and people still argue about what it means.
helena-fourment-in-a-fur-robe
A woman stands holding a dark fur robe closed around her. Peter Paul Rubens painted his young wife, Helena, in about 1638, and she wears nothing beneath the fur.
isaac-blessing-jacob
A blind old man puts his hand on his son's head to bless him, while his wife watches, in a warm, shadowy room. Govert Flinck painted it in 1638, and he was a student of Rembrandt's.
lord-john-stuart-and-his-brother-lord-bernard-stuart
Two young brothers stand in elegant silver and gold clothes, one with a hand on his hip. Anthony van Dyck painted them in about 1638, and both were killed in the English Civil War.
amor-and-psyche
The god Cupid and the girl Psyche lie together and sleep, in a soft, peaceful scene. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1639.
jacobs-dream
Jacob sleeps on the ground with a stone for a pillow, and a vision of a ladder with angels appears above him. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1639.
landscape-with-the-embarkation-of-saint-paula-romana-at
People board a ship at a busy harbor at sunrise, with big stone buildings and golden light. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1639.
landscape-with-the-finding-of-moses
A tiny group of people find a baby in a basket among the reeds on the river bank in a calm, golden landscape. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1639, and the baby is Moses.
the-martyrdom-of-saint-philip
Saint Philip is lifted onto a cross with a rope while a crowd of men look on, in a dark, dramatic scene. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1639.
joseph-and-potiphar-s-wife
Joseph hurries away, leaving his cloak behind, as a woman tries to hold him back, and a servant watches from the door. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1640.
malle-babbe

An old woman with a wild look and a big beer mug laughs loudly as an owl sits on her shoulder. Frans Hals painted it in about 1640, and Malle Babbe, meaning Crazy Babbe, was a real woman from Haarlem.
self-portrait-at-the-age-of-34

A confident young man in a fine dark coat and big hat leans on a stone sill and looks right at us. Rembrandt painted it in 1640 when he was 34, and he made himself look like a rich gentleman in a Renaissance portrait.
the-bean-king

A big, jolly family and their friends crowd around a table to celebrate Twelfth Night, with a man in a paper crown shouting 'The king drinks!' Jacob Jordaens painted it in about 1640, and the person who got the bean in their cake was king for the night.
the-presentation-in-the-temple
Mary offers her baby to a priest in a grand temple, with a crowd of onlookers. Simon Vouet painted it in 1640.
the-virgin-in-prayer
Mary, in a dark blue cloak, bows her head and clasps her hands in prayer, against a plain background. Sassoferrato painted it in about 1640, and the deep blue color, made from lapis lazuli, is rich.
portrait-of-a-girl-dressed-in-blue

A little girl in a bright blue silk dress and a lace collar holds a feather fan, looking out seriously. Johannes Cornelisz Verspronck painted it in 1641, and the fabric and lace are painted in loving detail.
saint-mary-of-egypt
An old woman with weathered skin and a long cloak looks up to heaven in the desert, with her hands clasped. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1641.
seaport-with-the-embarkation-of-saint-ursula
A harbor with tall buildings is lit by a low, glowing sun, while Saint Ursula and her friends board ships. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1641, and the sun's light on the water is amazing.
magdalene-with-the-smoking-flame
Mary Magdalene sits with a skull in her lap, and her face is lit by a candle flame with its smoke trailing up. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1642.
the-clubfoot

A smiling boy with a twisted foot holds a paper that says 'Give me alms for the love of God,' over his shoulder like a crutch. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1642, and he treated the poor boy with respect and warmth.
the-night-watch

A company of citizen soldiers in Amsterdam marches out with a flag and drum, with a little girl glowing in gold in the middle. Rembrandt painted it in 1642, and the name comes from a dark layer of varnish, but it is really a daytime scene.
the-abduction-of-europa-jordaens
A girl rides on the back of a bull as he walks into the sea, with her friends reaching out to her. Jacob Jordaens painted it in about 1643.
the-trojan-women-setting-fire-to-their-fleet
Women set fire to their own ships on a beach, to stop the long journey, as the sun sets over the sea. Claude Lorrain painted it in about 1643, and the story is from Virgil's Aeneid.
rokeby-venus

A woman reclines on a bed with her back to us, while Cupid holds a mirror, and her face is blurred in the reflection. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1644, and it is the only surviving nude by him. In 1914, a suffragette slashed it with a knife.
the-newborn
A mother and a nurse look at a swaddled newborn baby by the light of a single candle. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1645, and the glow is warm and quiet.
saint-januarius-leaves-the-furnace
A bishop saint steps unharmed out of a burning furnace, with angels lifting his robe. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1646.
sunrise
The sun rises over a bay, with ships and sailors in a golden, hazy light. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1646, and he was the master of painting glowing skies.
the-bull

A big black and white bull stands in a field in front of a farmer, a ram and a few cows. Paulus Potter painted it in 1647 when he was only 22, and it is life-size, so large that it was once thought to be too big to hang.
portrait-of-helena-van-der-schalcke
A little girl in a pretty dress sits on a chair, holding a little dog, with a calm, serious look. Gerard ter Borch painted it in about 1648.
the-embarkation-of-the-queen-of-sheba
A queen goes down a grand flight of steps to board a ship in a sunny harbor with huge buildings. Claude Lorrain painted it in 1648, and the glow of the low sun lights the whole port.
the-funeral-of-phocion
Two men carry a dead general's body in a stretcher through a stunning landscape, with a city in the distance. Nicolas Poussin painted it in 1648, and the people at the scene hide in the distance.
landscape-with-polyphemus
A giant, Polyphemus, plays a flute high on a mountain, behind a green, mythical landscape with nymphs and a shepherd. Nicolas Poussin painted it in 1649, and the giant is almost hidden in the rocks.
